verses.1: And for three years, there was no war between Arabia and Israel.
verses.2: In the third year, Jehosaphat, king of Judah, went to see King Israel.
verses.3: And the king of Israel said to his servants, “You know that Gilad is a high place for us. We intend to take it from the king of Aram.”
verses.4: And Joshua said to him, “Go with me into the battle at Ramot Gilad.” Then Joshua said to the king of Israel, “Just as I am, so shall you be; just as my people are, so shall you be. Just as my army is, so shall your army be.”
verses.5: And Josaphat said to the king of Israel, “Please hear what the LORD has said today.”
verses.6: And the king of Israel gathered together the prophets, four hundred in number. He said to them, “Go and fight against Gilad on the hill. If you fail, then say, ‘Come and take my life into your hands.’”
verses.7: And Josaphat said, “Is there no prophet of the LORD anymore? We must seek him from his face.”
verses.8: And the king of Israel said to Joshua, “Let there be one man who can ask God for guidance. I do not desire any good for him, only evil. Choose from among your people.” Then Joshua said, “Do not say, ‘The king wants it.’”
verses.9: And the king of Israel called one of Saris’ men and said, “Come here, Micaiah son of Imla.”
verses.10: And the kings of Israel and Judah sit on their thrones. They are dressed in fine clothes. All the prophets come before them.
verses.11: And Tzidkiah of Kenaanah made iron horns for him. He said, “As the Lord has said, ‘I will destroy the land of Aram until it is completely destroyed.’”
verses.12: And all the prophets were sent forth in this manner: “Go up to Gilgal, and succeed in your mission. Then Jehovah will give it into the hands of the king.”
verses.13: And the angel who went to call Michael, spoke to him and said, “Please, let me hear the words of the prophets. May their words be good for the king. Let your words be just as good as theirs.”
verses.14: And Micah said, “May the LORD live! For He who says, ‘The LORD has spoken to me,’ I will indeed speak.”
verses.15: And he went before the king. The king said to him, “Micaiah, go to Ramoth Gilead for battle. If you fail, then I will give you another opportunity.” But Micaiah replied, “Please let me go, and may God grant me success in this battle.”
verses.16: And the king said to him, “How many times must I praise you, since you never speak to me but only say the truth in the name of Jehovah?”
verses.17: And he said, “I saw all of Israel scattering into the mountains like sheep without a shepherd. Then God said, ‘Let no one return home in peace.’”
verses.18: And the king of Israel said to Joshua, “Did I not say to you that no good thing would ever happen to me, except for evil?”
verses.19: And he said to them, “Hear the word of the LORD. I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the armies in heaven stood around Him on His right and left.”
verses.20: And the LORD said, “Who will bless Ahazib? Who will make him rise and fall in Gilgal? He said, ‘This person will speak in Koah, and that person will speak in Koah.’”
verses.21: And the wind arose, and stood before Jehovah. He said, “I have sinned.” And Jehovah said to him, “In the hundredth place.”
verses.22: And he said, “I will go forth, and I will become a false spirit among all his prophets.” And he said, “Speak, and also act accordingly.”
verses.23: And now, behold, Jehovah has given false spirits into the mouths of all your prophets. And Jehovah has spoken evil against you.
verses.24: And Zidkiah, son of Kenaanah, went forward and struck Micheiah on the chest. Then he said, “Now the Spirit of Jehovah has passed over from me to speak with you.”
verses.25: And Michiah said, “You see that day when you will enter a house in order to worship.”
verses.26: And the king of Israel said, “Take Michas and return him to Amnon, the governor of the city, and to Joash, son of the king.”
verses.27: And you said, “As the king said, let them put this in the house of the treasury. Let them give it to them as bread and water, until they die in peace.”
verses.28: And Michai said, “If you return in peace, then the LORD will not speak against me.” And he said, “Let all nations hear this.”
verses.29: And the king of Israel rose up to judge, along with the king of Judah. Ramot Gilad was their place of judgment.
verses.30: And the king of Israel said to Joshua, “Arise and go into battle. You shall be my armor bearer.” So the king of Israel arose and went into battle.
verses.31: And the king of Aram ordered the commanders of his army, who numbered thirty-two in total, to say, “Do not fight against the small ones and the great ones. For only the king of Israel alone should fight.”
verses.32: And it happened that the officers of the army saw Joshua. They said, “But only King Israel can fight against them.” Then they refused to let him fight. And Joshua cried out in pain.
verses.33: And it seemed that the rulers of the chariot were not the king of Israel. So they turned away from him.
verses.34: And a man rushed forward, trying to get close to the king of Israel. He struck the king of Israel between the ribs and the sides of his body. Then he said to his horseman, “Turn your hand over, and I will be rescued from this situation.”
verses.35: And the battle took place on that day. The king was sitting in his chariot, with Aram present. He died in the afternoon, and his blood flowed onto the ground of the chariot.
verses.36: And the storm passed through the camp, as the sun rose. It was said, “One person went to his city, and another went to his land.”
verses.37: And the king died. Then Shomeron came and buried the king in Shomron.
verses.38: And he swept the chariot over with the words of Shomeron. The dogs licked his blood, and the women washed his body according to what Yahweh had commanded.
verses.39: And all the words of Ahau, and everything he did, and the house of the Shunn that he built, and all the cities he built—all these are recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.40: And Ahaziah slept with his fathers. And Ahaziah’s son, Jehoahaz, became king after him.
verses.41: Josaphat, son of Asa, became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahaz’s reign as king of Israel.
verses.42: He ruled for thirty-five and five years as king. He also ruled for forty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Azubah, daughter of Shilhiah.
verses.43: And Asa, his father, went everywhere, never failing to do what was right in the eyes of Jehovah.
verses.44: But the idols still continued to be worshipped and venerated by the people.
verses.45: And Josaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
verses.46: And all the words of Josaphat and his reign, what he did and what he fought against, are not written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.47: And the sacred remnant that remained during the time of his father Ahasuerus, in a land far from here.
verses.48: And there is no king other than Adonai.
verses.49: Yehoshaphat did what was right. He decided to go to Ophir for gold. But he didn’t go, because the people were in a difficult situation.
verses.50: Then Ahaziah son of Ahaz said to Jehosaphat, “Let my servants go with your servants in chariots and horses. I will not go with Jehosaphat.”
verses.51: And Joshua lay down with his ancestors. He was buried in the city of David, his father’s city. His son, Jeroboam, became king after him.
verses.52: Ahaziah, son of Ahaz, was king over Israel in Samaria. He ruled for seventeen years, during the time that Jehoash was king of Judah. He ruled over Israel for two years.
verses.53: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD. He followed the path of his father and mother, and also the path of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray.
verses.54: And she served her husband, and she bowed down to him. She also angered Yahweh, the God of Israel, just as her father had done.
